column2: req_desc

Scroll-scene storefront
The home page stacks the four scenes from Screens and layout, and every scene's heading and message is readable at every published viewport, with and without reduced motion.

Can turntable
A 3D can generated in code turns with pointer drag, swipe, scroll and the turn buttons, reports its flavour and angle in its accessible name, and falls back to a layered drawing of the can without WebGL, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Closed panels are inert
A closed cart drawer, mobile menu or FAQ answer is hidden from view, from the tab order and from the accessibility tree at every viewport.

Live flavour cards
Each flavour card shows its can price and its stock-left count, and open pages pick up stock changes without a reload within the delay stated in Business rules.

Crate Drop add sequence
Adding a flavour plays the lift, flight, pending outline, fill, counter roll, meter fill and stock-drop sequence from Motion and effects into the lowest-numbered empty slot.

Refused reservation return
When the server refuses a reservation, the can token flies back to its card, the slot stays empty, and a sold-out refusal adds a sold-out badge to the card that does not rely on colour alone.

Removing a can
Removing a can empties only that slot and releases its reservation. The counter rolls down, the meter drops, and every other can keeps its slot.

Crate announcements
Every add, refusal, removal and hold expiry is announced in the `Crate updates` live region with the exact copy from Feedback states.

Crate layout by viewport
The crate is a 3-by-4 grid in a bottom sheet on phones, a side panel on tablets and a fixed rail beside the flavour carousel on desktops, as laid out in Screens and layout, with no horizontal overflow.

Reduced-motion crate
With reduced motion requested, the crate skips the lift, flight and overshoot, shows the pending outline at once, fades the slot to filled on confirmation, and steps the counter and meter, as qualified in Motion and effects.

Keyboard crate and cart drawer
Adding cans, removing a can from a focused slot, and opening, working and closing the cart drawer all work by keyboard alone, as described in Interactions.

Quote endpoint
`POST /api/quote` returns the exact-cent breakdown for any supported province, can mix and subscribe choice, and rejects bad input as specified in API.

Discount, deposit and tax arithmetic
Discount, deposit and tax follow the money rules in Business rules, including half-up rounding once per tax line and largest-remainder allocation of the discount across lines.

Free-shipping threshold
Shipping is free exactly when discounted goods reach the destination province's threshold, and the meter percentage and remaining amount always equal the server quote.

Live totals panel
Changing the province, the crate contents or the subscribe-and-save switch updates every totals row in place to the server's quote within the delay stated in Business rules, and a province or switch change announces the new total.

Reservation holds
Each can in a crate is a server reservation. All of a crate's reservations share one hold window that starts at the first reserve, within the per-crate limits in Business rules.

One winner for the last cans
When simultaneous reservations compete for the last available cans, only as many succeed as there are cans left, and reserved plus sold never exceeds the released quantity.

Server-side hold expiry
The server ends a hold at its expiry instant and releases its cans even while the shopper's page is still open, and refuses checkout on that hold from that instant, as qualified in Business rules.

Cart stays put through the countdown
Countdown ticks and live stock updates never close the cart drawer, move focus, clear typed fields or change the checkout step until the server reports the hold expired.

Stock ledger
Every stock change is a ledger event, and the staff stock view shows received, sold, returned, on-hand, reserved, available and released figures that satisfy the ledger identities in Business rules.

Customer accounts and addresses
Shoppers sign up and sign in with PocketBase-backed accounts and keep saved Canadian shipping addresses, with exactly one default per account.

Checkout once per attempt
Replaying a checkout with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the original response and never charges twice, and reusing a key with a different body is refused, as specified in Business rules.

Paid order record set
A paid order has exactly one Kill Bill payment for its total, one invoice PDF, one packing-slip PDF and one confirmation email, as qualified for mail outages in Services.

Thank-you route
After payment is confirmed, the browser lands on the order's thank-you route, and reloading or opening that address shows the same confirmation to the order's owner.

Keyboard checkout
A shopper can go from the crate to the thank-you page by keyboard alone, and an error summary links to each invalid field.

Private data stays out of copies
Emails, invoice PDFs and packing slips never contain card data, provider identifiers, tokens or another customer's address.

Order history and documents
Customers list their own orders and download their own invoice PDFs, and another customer's order is treated as unknown.

Subscribe and save
Checking out an eligible crate with subscribe-and-save on creates a Kill Bill subscription on the matching published plan and a first paid order at the discounted price.

Subscription page mirrors Kill Bill
The subscription page and API show only Kill Bill's confirmed state, next renewal date and end date.

Pause and resume
Subscribers pause deliveries for 1 to 3 boxes or resume early, and each pause or resume is recorded as a Kill Bill blocking state, as qualified in Business rules.

Skip and flavour swap
Subscribers skip the next box or swap to another box with the same delivery rhythm, and Kill Bill records a one-cycle block or a plan change.

Cancel at end of term
Cancelling ends the subscription on Kill Bill's charged-through date and never earlier, and the subscription page shows that date.

Pending changes
Each subscription change shows as pending until Kill Bill confirms it, cannot be submitted again while pending, and ends as applied or rejected.

Change cutoff
A pause, skip or swap requested at or after the change cutoff applies to the following cycle, and the page says so.

Landing after a subscription change
Saving any subscription change returns the browser to the subscription's page with the change shown as pending or applied, and a card update returns there with its card status message instead, as qualified in Feedback states.

Subscription emails
Each confirmed pause, skip, swap and cancel, each successful renewal and each upcoming renewal sends exactly one email with the subject from Services.

Renewal charging
The server charges each new Kill Bill renewal invoice to the card on file, creates a paid renewal order on success and starts dunning on failure, within the delay stated in Business rules.

Dunning schedule
A failed renewal is retried on days 1, 3 and 7. Shipments are held on day 8 and the subscription is cancelled on day 14, with one dunning email per step and the day length taken from the environment, as qualified in Business rules.

Dunning banner
A subscriber in dunning sees the published dunning banner for their dunning stage, word for word.

Card update recovery
Updating the card while past due charges the open renewal at once. If the charge succeeds, the subscription is active again and any shipment hold is lifted.

Fulfilment queue and order states
Fulfilment staff work paid orders oldest first through picking, packed and shipped, and every illegal transition is refused.

Packing slips
Each paid order has one packing-slip PDF, written once to the file store and served only to staff.

Queue layout switch
The fulfilment queue shows order cards below the published width and a table at that width and wider.

Staff outage banner
Every back-office page shows the published outage banner for each unreachable service, word for word.

Role-limited actions
The server refuses every staff and owner endpoint to roles outside its published role list, so fulfilment staff cannot refund but can still mark orders packed.

Full refund
A full refund returns the whole refundable amount through Kill Bill and puts the cans back in stock when the order had not shipped.

Partial refund split
A partial refund splits its amount across line goods, line deposits, shipping and tax lines by largest remainder, and never exceeds what is left to refund.

Provider-confirmed refunds
A refund shows as pending until Kill Bill confirms it. Only then does it change the order's refund status and send the refund email.

Prices and shipping thresholds
The owner edits the limited drop's can price and each province's shipping rate and free-shipping threshold, and the next quote uses them.

Drop release quantity
The owner sets how many limited-drop cans are released, and the server refuses any quantity below the cans already held or sold.

Owner dashboard
The owner dashboard shows dunning recovery and refunds for the last 30 days and the live status of each service.

Reviews
Customers who bought a flavour can review it, and an approved review appears on open flavour pages without a reload within the delay stated in Business rules.

Points of sale
The stockists page lists the five nearest points of sale to a chosen city or to the shopper's location, with distances.

Retailer application
An applicant's business licence file is stored in the file store before the application is recorded, and the applicant then lands on the application's page.

Application review
The owner approves or declines each submitted application exactly once, and the applicant receives one decision email.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from its run manifest on the published port and answers the health check.

Service outages
When any one service is unreachable, the endpoints that need it answer the published status and body, and the rest of the app keeps working. Email queued while the mail server is unreachable is sent exactly once, as qualified in Services.

Server boundary
The server accepts same-origin requests only, enforces the published body limits, and never serves source files or credentials.

Configuration from environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start, never hard-coded, and never sent to the browser.

Look and composition
The storefront and back office follow the palette, type, composition and botanical drawing described in Visual design.
`/app/run.json` exists with string fields `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and the app starts only through it.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` lists every shipped package, font and icon set with its licence. "Shipped packages" means the production dependency tree reported by `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`.
Every shipped package is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0 or CC0-1.0, and every font is under OFL-1.1.
No datastore beyond Postgres, PocketBase, MinIO, Kill Bill and Mailpit holds app state: no SQLite, Redis, local JSON files or in-memory state that must survive a restart.
The provided service configuration and environment files stay unchanged.
Fonts, icons and scripts are served from the app itself, and no page loads a resource from a third-party host at runtime.
The repository holds no imported 3D model files (`.glb`, `.gltf`, `.obj`, `.fbx`). The can is generated in code.
Application source is TypeScript. Hand-written JavaScript appears only in config files.
